name: María Corina Machado
role: Venezuelan opposition leader, Vente Venezuela coordinator, National Assembly member (2011–2014), Nobel Peace Prize laureate (2025)
summary: Machado is a market-liberal, anti-socialist opposition leader who campaigns for privatising Venezuela's oil industry and state firms, protecting private property and restoring democratic elections. She has backed US pressure and military action against the Maduro government, supports Israel, and holds socially moderate views (exceptions to an abortion ban, same-sex unions or marriage, medical cannabis).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Her Freedom Manifesto says the state should only create conditions for a free and competitive economy and that the state's heavy hand on the market stifles growth; in 2023 she called her model non-socialist and said socialism subordinates society to the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Her programme and her own remarks call for privatising all oil and gas production, PDVSA and more than 500 state-held companies, with the state only as regulator.

property-fundamental.rationale: Manifesto: a renewed Venezuela guarantees the right to property and to recover what was stolen, as a fundamental right; in 2012 she told Chavez on live television that expropriation is theft.

strong-leader.rationale: Nobel speech criticises the notion that charisma can substitute for the rule of law.

state-harmful.rationale: Describes the state's purpose as safeguarding natural rights and enabling a free economy; wants a limited state, not no state.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Reported 2023 positions: support for same-sex marriage (some outlets say civil unions); I could not open her original interview.

abortion-legal.rationale: Personally opposed; advocates decriminalising abortion in cases of rape and a debate for risk to the mother's life, not legal in most cases.

more-religion-public.rationale: She says she believes in God but rules out letting her faith shape her politics.

free-trade.rationale: Programme proposes opening trade channels with the world and simplifying trade policy; she pledged open markets and the Manifesto calls for alliances based on trade and shared prosperity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Has advocated foreign intervention to remove Maduro on humanitarian grounds, called escalating pressure the only way, and welcomed the US strikes.

central-planning.rationale: Programme aims to remove state economic controls she says only fed corruption; she describes socialism as producing misery.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Her plan leaves investment to private capital with the state as a regulator rather than directing strategic industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Campaigned in 2011 on "popular capitalism"; analysts describe the aim as making citizens shareholders of industries. The programme details are secondhand.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nobel speech celebrates a plural society united across parties, unions and civil society and condemns the regime's dismantling of democracy.

democracy-best.rationale: Nobel speech frames democracy as essential to peace and says the mandate belongs to the people; she organised a primary and an election defence on that basis.

separate-church-state.rationale: She keeps her faith out of politics and praised religious liberty in the 1811 constitution; no direct statement on strict separation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Nobel speech says her generation cherished rights but forgot duties; the Manifesto nonetheless stresses inalienable individual rights.

direct-action.rationale: After years of other strategies she chose the primary and defence of the vote as her route to change.

harm-principle.rationale: In 2023 she said each person has the right to make their own decisions, from educating children and investing to religious or sexual preferences.

total-state.rationale: Wants a limited state and a free economy, opposing state direction of the economy and society.

universal-morality.rationale: Manifesto speaks of eternal, inalienable rights belonging to every human being.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Expressed solidarity with Israel, signed a cooperation agreement with Likud and pledged to restore diplomatic relations; no explicit statement on the right to a state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Manifesto and Nobel speech promise to restore the right of the nine million Venezuelan emigrants to return home.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Programme proposes reducing the fiscal deficit and its monetary financing to stabilise the economy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Washington Post editors described her manifesto as directly linking political freedom with economic prosperity and property; she treats economic freedom as one of the freedoms to be restored.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Plan "Venezuela, Tierra de Gracia" aims to raise oil output sharply (toward three million barrels a day) and make Venezuela an energy hub; she presented it at CERAWeek.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nobel speech describes obscene corruption and looting by the rulers; she has also attacked the established opposition.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Manifesto says crimes against humanity must be judged by law; this concerns perpetrators of the regime more than a general rule.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Manifesto limits the state to securing rights and conditions for a free economy, but her programme also includes humanitarian aid, public services and infrastructure investment.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Nobel speech affirms that every human being carries sovereign dignity and describes societies of free and equal citizens; Manifesto proclaims the dignity of every human being.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Manifesto: the people are the only sovereign and government exists to serve citizens.

separated-powers.rationale: Nobel speech praises the 1811 constitution for enshrining separation of powers and condemns the regime for purging independent judges.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Programme presentation says current economic controls only served corruption and aims to remove them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Nobel speech lists press censorship among the regime's crimes; Manifesto demands speech free of censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: In 2023 she called for banning re-election to political office.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Programme proposes restructuring and agreeing terms with creditors and multilaterals rather than cancelling the debt.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Programme as presented by its economists calls for institutional independence of the Central Bank with inflation targets.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Pledged rule of law and condemns the regime for violating the constitution.

land-redistribution.rationale: Calls expropriation of private land and businesses theft, and her programme returns expropriated assets to their owners.

refugee-return.rationale: Promises that the displaced Venezuelans can return home; descendants are not addressed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Calls for opening trade and welcoming investors worldwide, not a closed bloc.

delink-world-market.rationale: Programme and statements aim to reintegrate Venezuela into world markets and financial markets and attract global investors.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Her Freedom Manifesto sets out inalienable rights and was described as a precursor to a new constitution; no explicit stance on amendment thresholds.

elective-rulers.rationale: Says mandates belong to the people and built her movement around free elections.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Leads a campaign to remove Maduro, whom she accuses of violating the constitution and stealing the 2024 vote.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Her plan depends on foreign investment, IMF/multilateral financing and market reintegration.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Her Manifesto frames freedom and rights as universal, belonging to every human being.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Seeks large foreign and domestic private investment, including in oil and gas, from the US, Europe, China and the Middle East.

democratic-peace.rationale: Nobel speech says democracy is essential to peace; no statement on democracies not fighting each other.

non-intervention.rationale: Has called for foreign pressure and intervention in Venezuela and welcomed US military action there.

defeat-communism.rationale: Openly anti-communist, signed the 2020 Madrid Charter and said she would bury socialism forever.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Campaigns for popular capitalism and against socialism and communism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nobel speech refers to Jews arriving after the Holocaust as historical fact.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemns persecution of dissent and imprisonment of opponents as regime crimes and promises to free political prisoners.

assisted-dying.rationale: One outlet reports she supports euthanasia in specific situations; not confirmed from her own words.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Vente says it breaks from the left-right argument; she said liberal proposals are neither left nor far right but what works.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Says rights are granted by the Creator but that the people are the only sovereign and authority rests on popular sovereignty.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Programme seeks an IMF-backed international financing programme with structural reforms and a debt agreement with creditors.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Pledged strict rule of law from day one and condemns violation of the constitution.

term-limits.rationale: In 2023 she called for banning re-election to political office.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Said the struggle of Venezuelans was an ethical struggle for truth and a spiritual struggle for good.

person-over-state.rationale: Manifesto: government serves its citizens and the supreme purpose of the state is to safeguard natural rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Describes her struggle as ethical, existential and spiritual and speaks of certainties of the soul; Manifesto calls freedom divinely given.

capital-controls.rationale: Programme proposes free convertibility of the currency and re-entering international financial markets.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Manifesto grounds rights and dignity in the nature of humanity.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Backed US strikes on suspected drug boats ("Finally, this is happening"), said deaths are Maduro's responsibility and, asked about due process, described a very cruel war.

close-ties-china.rationale: Welcomes Chinese investment on fair terms but frames her alliance with the US and criticises ties of Venezuela's rulers to China, Russia and Iran.

national-resource-control.rationale: Plans privatising oil with foreign investors while the state keeps regulation, royalties and taxes; the evidence cuts both ways on national control.

notes: Most recent positions used (2023-2026). On same-sex marriage, outlets differ between civil unions and marriage, and I could not open her original 2023 interview. Several sites (The Hill, Times of Israel, Reuters, Sky News, Expreso) blocked access, so Israel and strike positions rest partly on Wikipedia. No full text of the Vente programme or Freedom Manifesto was reachable; the manifesto and programme are cited through news reports quoting them.
